A chromatography column, packed with silica gel as stationary phase, was used to separate a
mixture of compounds consisting of (A) benzanilide (B) aniline and (C) acetophenone. When the
column is eluted with a mixture of solvents, hexane : ethyl acetate (20:80), the sequence of
obtained compounds is :
en.explanation:
Silica gel is a polar adsorbent with acidic groups; a compound is held back in proportion to how strongly it adsorbs by hydrogen bonding and dipolar interaction, and the least strongly adsorbed compound leaves the column first.

Acetophenone, , has no bond and only accepts hydrogen bonds through its carbonyl oxygen, so it is held least and elutes first.

Benzanilide, , has a single flanked by two phenyl rings, and its nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the carbonyl group, so it is held moderately.

Aniline, , has two bonds and a basic nitrogen lone pair that binds to the acidic silanol groups, so it is held most and elutes last.

Order of elution: acetophenone, benzanilide, aniline, that is (C), (A), (B).

Hence, the correct option is (C).
